style_block: Warm archival documentary photography style evoking mid-twentieth-century American broadcast television and radio, shot on grainy film stock, soft sepia-toned grading in the earliest scenes that gradually shifts warmer and more saturated as the timeline moves from the 1930s toward the 2000s, gentle vignette, soft chromatic aberration at frame edges, subtle film scratches and dust, period-accurate wardrobe and set design, radio studio microphones, television soundstages, network office interiors, cinematic 16:9 composition framed like a classic broadcast-history documentary. All people depicted are archetypal, fictionalized, stylized figures representative of their era and role rather than an exact reproduction or likeness of any real named individual. No modern technology, no smartphones, no flat screen displays, no exact photographic likeness of any real person, no photorealistic reproduction of real world logos or trademarked packaging text, no watermark, no signature, no extra fingers, no distorted limbs, no garbled or misspelled lettering, no text anywhere in the image.

characters.CREATOR: an archetypal 1930s female radio writer and producer character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real person, dark bobbed hair, a tailored high-collared blouse, often seated at a large studio microphone or a writing desk covered in script pages, thoughtful expression
characters.MINISTER: a fictional 1930s radio drama character, an elderly widowed minister, silver hair, wire-frame glasses, a dark clergy suit, usually seated in a warmly lit study beside a small lit desk lamp
characters.LEAD_ACTRESS: an archetypal soap opera leading actress character who plays the same role for decades, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real person, expressive features, glamorous period-appropriate wardrobe that subtly ages across decades, usually on a soap opera soundstage set
characters.NETWORK_EXEC: an archetypal late-2000s television network executive character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real person, gray suit, seated behind a cluttered office desk covered in ratings printouts

reference_notes: Niche research showed the strongest classic-TV nostalgia channels leaning on real archival photography, which this pipeline cannot reproduce (no real photo sourcing, and no exact likeness of real named actors). Chose a vintage film/TV grain documentary treatment instead - era-accurate grading that visibly ages across the 1937-2009 timeline - with every named real person (Irna Phillips, Kevin Bacon, Calista Flockhart, James Earl Jones, Cicely Tyson, Allison Janney, Hayden Panettiere, Kim Zimmer) rendered as an archetypal, stylized figure rather than a likeness, the same approach used for real people in earlier videos in this pipeline. Only figures appearing across many scenes (the creator, the fictional minister character, the decades-spanning lead actress, and the cancellation-era network executive) get a persistent character key; one-scene cameos (Bacon, Flockhart, Jones, Tyson, Janney, Panettiere) are described inline per scene instead, since they do not recur.
